findings.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — (P1, conf 100) `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)` requires the user to be both admin and owner, so team ADMINs (non-owners) who manage the event type get FORBIDDEN; the permission check should be `||` (and an eventType without a team falls back to teamId 0 instead of skipping the team check).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — (P1, conf 100) the handler never checks booking status or endTime, so guests get added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings and are sent `status: "CONFIRMED"` / `method: "REQUEST"` invites for a meeting that is not happening; the only guard is the UI hiding the action.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — (P2, conf 100) the dedup check `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive and guests are never lowercased, so `Bob@x.com` gets added again next to an existing `bob@x.com` attendee, creating a duplicate Attendee row, calendar invitee and email.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — (P2, conf 100) the blacklist is lowercased (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but `guest` is not, so any blacklisted address typed with a capital letter gets past `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — (P2, conf 100) the server schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no uniqueness or max-length rule (only the client refine in AddGuestsDialog.tsx:26 checks uniqueness, and case-sensitively), so a direct API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` passes the filter and `createMany` inserts duplicate attendees, and an unbounded list fans out unbounded emails.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — (P2, conf 75) check-then-insert is not atomic and Attendee has no unique (bookingId, email) constraint, so two concurrent addGuests calls (double-click, two hosts) both pass the `booking.attendees.some` filter on stale data and both insert the same guest.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — (P1, conf 75) EventManager is built from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (the caller's credentials) while the `booking.user.credentials` loaded at line 38 go unused, so when a team admin or attendee adds guests, `updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` cannot match `booking.references[].credentialId` to the organizer's calendar credential, and the organizer's calendar event is not updated (or the update goes through the wrong account).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — (P1, conf 100) the attendee rows are committed at line 92 before the unguarded `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`; if the calendar update throws, the client sees an error while the guests stay in the DB, no emails go out, and a retry fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid` because every guest now counts as a duplicate, leaving DB and calendar permanently out of sync.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — (P2, conf 100) `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` gets the raw input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee whose email was in the submitted list is matched by `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (email-manager.ts:541) and gets a fresh "booking scheduled" email as if newly invited, and email failures are swallowed with `console.log` while the mutation reports success.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:138 — (P2, conf 75) for recurring bookings the evt carries the series `recurringEvent` (the calendar event and ICS invite cover the whole series), but `createMany` adds attendees only to this one occurrence's Booking row, so the other occurrences in the `recurringEventId` series lack the guest in the DB (reschedule, cancel and reminder flows skip them).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — (P2, conf 75) guests are written straight into `attendees` with no seat or BookingSeat handling, even though the handler forwards `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees`, so on seated event types they skip seat capacity accounting and (with seatsShowAttendees off) are handled differently from attendees who booked a seat.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — (P2, conf 75) the rebuilt CalendarEvent leaves out `team`, `iCalUID`/sequence, `responses` and `customInputs`, so the `calendarEvent.team?.members` branch in sendAddGuestsEmails (email-manager.ts:531) never runs (collective hosts are not notified), and the new REQUEST ICS may not match the original invite UID, so existing attendees' mail clients create a second event instead of updating the first.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — (P2, conf 75) any attendee (matched by case-sensitive primary `user.email` only) may add unlimited guests who then get invites sent in the organizer's name, with no organizer opt-in or event-type setting (the `disableGuests` booking field is ignored), which widens the permission model beyond editLocation/requestReschedule (organizer-only).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:84 — (P3, conf 75) new guests are stored with `name: ""` and the organizer's timeZone/locale, so the emails address them as ` <email>` and show times and language in the organizer's zone, and later flows treat those placeholder values as real attendee data.

packages/emails/email-manager.ts:525 — P1/conf100 SIBLING-FLAG-PROPAGATION: `export const sendAddGuestsEmails = async (calEvent: CalendarEvent, newGuests: string[])` takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and never calls `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, unlike the adjacent `sendLocationChangeEmails` (line 495) and every other booking email path, so event types with `metadata.disableStandardEmails.all.host` or `.attendee` set still get host and attendee emails whenever guests are added (the handler at addGuests.handler.ts:168 `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` doesn't pass `booking.eventType?.metadata` either).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — P2/conf50 SIBLING-FLAG-PROPAGATION: the `evt: CalendarEvent` built here leaves out `hideCalendarNotes` and `hideCalendarEventDetails` from the event type, and sendAddGuestsEmails doesn't apply the `...(formattedCalEvent.hideCalendarNotes && { additionalNotes: undefined })` stripping that sendScheduledEmails does, so the new emails, ICS files and calendar update ignore the event type's privacy settings (booking notes stored in `description: booking.description` go to every new guest).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:146 — P1/conf75 seated events aren't handled: guests are written with `attendees.createMany` without checking `seatsPerTimeSlot` capacity or creating BookingSeat references, and sendAddGuestsEmails sends AttendeeAddGuestsEmail with the full attendee list to every seat holder, so adding guests can overbook a seated slot and show seat holders to each other even when `seatsShowAttendees` is false (sibling `sendScheduledSeatsEmails` emails each seat separately).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — P1/conf100 the blacklist check doesn't normalize case: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the raw guest against a lowercased list, so `Blocked@Domain.com` gets past BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS; the existing-attendee check `guest === attendee.email` is also case-sensitive, so `Alice@x.com` is added again as a duplicate of `alice@x.com`.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — P2/conf100 `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no uniqueness refine and no `.min(1)` (only the client dialog checks for duplicates), and the handler's filter only compares against existing attendees, so an API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` inserts two Attendee rows for the same person and sends them two emails.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — P2/conf100 `uniqueGuests` doesn't exclude the organizer (`organizer.email` / `booking.userPrimaryEmail`) or team hosts, so the host can be added as an attendee of their own booking, which duplicates them in the calendar invite and sends them both an OrganizerAddGuestsEmail and an AttendeeScheduledEmail.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — P2/conf100 `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` gets the raw input `guests` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee whose email was re-submitted matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and gets a fresh "scheduled" confirmation email instead of the guests-added notice, and blacklisted emails are still used as the new-guest set.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:44 — P2/conf100 there's no check on booking status or time: after the NOT_FOUND check the handler goes straight to permissions, so guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings, and the UI offers it on past bookings too (BookingListItem.tsx:554 `{isBookingInPast && isConfirmed ? <TableActions actions={bookedActions} /> : null}` where bookedActions contains editBookingActions); new guests then get CONFIRMED invites for dead or finished meetings.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:138 — P1/conf75 recurring bookings aren't handled: only the single `bookingId` row gets the new attendees (other bookings sharing `recurringEventId` are left alone), but `recurringEvent: parseRecurringEvent(booking.eventType?.recurringEvent)` puts the series RRULE into the ICS and calendar update, so new guests receive an invite for the whole series while the database lists them on one occurrence only.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — P1/conf75 requiresConfirmation/PENDING bookings aren't considered: the handler never checks `booking.status`, the UI exposes the action for pending bookings, and new guests get `AttendeeScheduledEmail` plus an ICS with `status: "CONFIRMED"` for a booking the host hasn't accepted yet (sibling paths send AttendeeRequestEmail for this state).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — P1/conf75 the calendar event isn't updated when anyone other than the organizer adds guests: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({...user, ...})` use the caller's credentials, not the booking owner's (`booking.user.credentials` is fetched at line 38 and never used), so when a team admin or attendee adds guests, `updateCalendarAttendees` can't reach the organizer's external calendar event and the new guests never appear on the real invite.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:124 — P2/conf100 `evt` has no `team` field, so `calendarEvent.team?.members` in sendAddGuestsEmails is always undefined and co-hosts on collective/team bookings never get the OrganizerAddGuestsEmail, even though the team-member loop was copied from the sibling path.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — P2/conf75 `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires the caller to be both admin and owner, so a team admin who isn't the owner (and isn't the organizer or an attendee) gets FORBIDDEN, and the requirement that team admins can manage guests on team bookings isn't met.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:55 — P3/conf100 the i18n key `you_do_not_have_permission` doesn't exist in apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json (only `dont_have_permission` does), so the dialog's `t(err.message)` toast shows the raw key "FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission".

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:1 — P1/conf100 the diff has no tests: no unit tests for addGuestsHandler (permissions, dedupe, blacklist, empty list), none for sendAddGuestsEmails recipient selection and flag gating, and no Playwright coverage for the new `data-testid="add_members"` dialog, so none of the acceptance criteria are checked.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — P2/conf50 advisory: sibling attendee-changing paths (reschedule, location change, seat booking) also fire BOOKING webhooks and schedule workflow reminders for attendees, but this path does neither, so webhook subscribers never learn about the new attendees and new guests get no workflow reminder emails or SMS.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P2/conf75: dual-write gap — `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: { data: guestsFullDetails } } } })` inserts Attendee rows but never merges the new emails into `booking.responses.guests`, so the two stores of guest data diverge and any flow that rebuilds attendees from `responses` (reschedule prefill/re-create, booking success page, webhooks/workflows reading responses) silently drops the added guests.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:87 — P3/conf75: field-fidelity — guest Attendee rows are persisted with `timeZone: organizer.timeZone, locale: organizer.locale` (and `name: ""` at :85), so guests added by an attendee in another region are stored permanently with the organizer's timezone/locale, and every later email/reminder/ICS for those rows renders times and language in the wrong zone/locale with a blank name.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — P2/conf75: duplicate Attendee rows — dedupe uses case-sensitive `guest === attendee.email` and never dedupes within `guests` itself (server schema at addGuests.schema.ts:5 is `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness; the refine exists only client-side), and there is no (bookingId,email) unique constraint, so `John@x.com` vs existing `john@x.com`, a repeated email in one payload, or two concurrent requests each insert duplicate attendee rows for the same person.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — P2/conf75: re-run-unsafe non-atomic write — attendee rows are committed at :92 before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs outside any transaction, so if the calendar update throws the DB holds guests the external calendar event never received, and a retry is rejected at :80-81 with `emails_must_be_unique_valid` because the guests now already exist, leaving the divergence unrecoverable through this endpoint.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P2/conf50: seated-event integrity — for bookings with `seatsPerTimeSlot` set (read at :145) the handler creates Attendee rows with no corresponding BookingSeat rows, producing seat-less attendees that inflate the attendee-based seat count past capacity and are orphaned from seat cancel/reschedule flows keyed on BookingSeat.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:92 — P3/conf50: recurring-series divergence — only the single booking `id: bookingId` receives new attendees while the calendar event built with `recurringEvent: parseRecurringEvent(...)` (:138) is updated for the whole series, so sibling bookings sharing `recurringEventId` lack the guest Attendee rows that the external calendar shows on every occurrence.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user); const eventManager = new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` builds EventManager from the CALLER's credentials instead of the booking organizer's (`booking.user.credentials` is fetched at line 38 and never used), so when an attendee or team owner adds guests, the booking.references credentialIds do not resolve to any loaded calendar credential and the organizer's external calendar event is not updated with the new attendees (P2, conf 50).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` runs uncaught after the `prisma.booking.update` attendee insert at line 92 has already committed, so any calendar-provider failure returns an error to the dialog while guests are persisted, and the user's retry is rejected with BAD_REQUEST "emails_must_be_unique_valid" because the guests now already exist as attendees (P2, conf 50).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);` passes the raw `guests` input rather than the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee whose email is re-submitted alongside a new guest is classified as a "new guest" in email-manager.ts `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` and receives a duplicate AttendeeScheduledEmail booking confirmation instead of the AttendeeAddGuestsEmail notice (P3, conf 75).

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — (P1, confidence 75) `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` + `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` builds the calendar updater from the acting user's credentials rather than the booking organizer's (`booking.user.credentials` is fetched but never used), so when an attendee or team owner adds guests (both explicitly permitted at lines 46-55) the organizer's calendar event referenced by `booking.references` is not updated and the new guests never receive a real calendar invite, while the DB and toast say "Guests added".

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — (P1, confidence 50) `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` calls an EventManager method that this diff never adds (packages/core/EventManager.ts is untouched), so if it does not already exist the call throws after `prisma.booking.update` has already persisted the guests, which means no calendar update and no emails, the UI shows an error, and the guests stay stored on the booking without ever being notified.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — (P2, confidence 75) `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` swallows email failure and still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so the dialog tells the organizer the guests were added even though they got no email, and that email is their only invite whenever the calendar update above did not reach them.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — (P2, confidence 100) the handler passes the raw `guests` input to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee whose email is resubmitted matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts:541) and gets a fresh "event scheduled" confirmation (AttendeeScheduledEmail) as if newly booked, not the "guests added" update notice.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:37 — (P3, confidence 75) the success toast `t("guests_added")` shows for every submitted email, but the handler silently drops blacklisted and already-present emails (addGuests.handler.ts:74-78), so the organizer is told guests were added who were never added or notified.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:138 — (P2, confidence 50) `recurringEvent: parseRecurringEvent(booking.eventType?.recurringEvent)` puts the series recurrence into the emails/ICS sent to new guests, but they are only inserted as attendees on this single occurrence's booking, so a guest added to one occurrence of a recurring booking gets an invite for the whole series while missing from every other occurrence.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — (P2, confidence 50) the handler never checks `booking.status` or end time, so a direct API call can add guests to a CANCELLED/REJECTED or past booking and send them a `status: "CONFIRMED"` REQUEST invite (AttendeeScheduledEmail) for a meeting that is not happening, which is not "guest management on existing bookings".

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:47 — (P3, confidence 50) `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`, so despite its name only team owners (not team admins) of a team event who are not the organizer can manage guests, which quietly narrows who the feature serves.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — (P1, conf 75) SILENT-PARTIAL-SUCCESS/non-atomic: attendees are committed by `prisma.booking.update({... createMany ...})` (line 101) before `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs outside any try/catch, so a throw in getUsersCredentials/EventManager returns a 500 with guests already persisted and no emails sent, and a retry is then rejected at line 80 with BAD_REQUEST "emails_must_be_unique_valid" because the guests now count as existing attendees, so they are never notified.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:165 — (P1, conf 75) UNHANDLED-ASYNC-FAILURE: `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` result is discarded, and EventManager.updateAllCalendarEvents catches each per-reference failure and returns `success: false` without throwing, so a failed Google/Outlook attendee update is swallowed and the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, leaving the external calendar event without the new guests.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — (P1, conf 50) CREDENTIAL-LIFECYCLE: the EventManager is built from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` (the caller) instead of the booking owner's credentials (`booking.user.credentials` is loaded at line 38 but never used), so when a team admin or attendee adds guests, any booking reference without a matching credentialId gets the caller's credential of that type (or none) and the calendar update fails or no-ops, which gets swallowed as in the finding above.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:170 — (P2, conf 100) UNHANDLED-ASYNC-FAILURE: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` throws away the error object and falls through to a success response, so SMTP/render failures are unobservable in logs and the client shows the "guests_added" toast even though no invitation reached the new guests; Promise.all also rejects on the first failure, so you can't tell which recipients got an email.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — (P2, conf 100) `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the raw `guests` input rather than the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so an email that was already an attendee and is submitted again matches `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (email-manager.ts:541) and gets a duplicate new-booking AttendeeScheduledEmail/ICS REQUEST instead of the guests-added notice.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:74 — (P2, conf 100) SILENT-PARTIAL-SUCCESS: `guests.filter(...)` quietly drops duplicate and blacklisted emails, yet the response is still `{ message: "Guests added" }` with no count or skipped list, so the user sees "Guests added" for addresses that were never added.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — (P2, conf 75) the duplicate check `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive (client uniqueness check too, AddGuestsDialog.tsx:27), so `Alice@x.com` and an existing `alice@x.com` both get inserted by createMany, and that attendee receives duplicate calendar invites and emails.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — (P2, conf 100) OUTBOUND-CALL-HARDENING: `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()`, so one request can insert any number of attendee rows, run getTranslation per attendee, push that many attendees into the external calendar update, and synchronously await one email per attendee plus organizer inside the request, which ends in request timeouts and provider rate-limit failures that the handler swallows.

packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25 — (P3, conf 75) unbounded per-recipient list growth: `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]` puts every attendee in the header of each organizer/team-member email, so header size grows O(attendees) per message (O(N x M) overall) with no cap, and large guest lists can hit SMTP header limits and get rejected, which is then swallowed at handler:170.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:58 — (P2, conf 75) ERROR-SHAPE-LEAKAGE: `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })` throws a Prisma NotFoundError (surfaces as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR 500) for bookings with a null/deleted owner instead of a TRPCError NOT_FOUND, and the dialog then shows the raw Prisma message.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:55 — (P3, conf 100) ERROR-SHAPE-LEAKAGE: the FORBIDDEN message key `you_do_not_have_permission` is missing from en/common.json, so the client's `t(err.message)` shows the literal key "FORBIDDEN: you_do_not_have_permission" instead of a translated message.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:43 — (P3, conf 100) `const message = \`${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}\`` always produces a truthy string, so the `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback never runs, and network/transport errors with no `err.data` show "undefined: <raw message>" (zod input errors show the raw JSON issue array).

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:49 — (P3, conf 100) OPTIMISTIC-STATE-DESYNC: if the user removes every row, `if (multiEmailValue.length === 0) return;` makes the Add button do nothing with no feedback, and a leftover empty "" row from "add another" fails `z.string().email()` and shows the wrong "emails must be unique and valid" error instead of ignoring the blank entry.

apps/web/components/dialog/AddGuestsDialog.tsx:36 — (P3, conf 100) OPTIMISTIC-STATE-DESYNC: `isInvalidEmail` is never cleared on edit, on success, or when the dialog closes via overlay/Escape (`onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`), so after a failed attempt then a successful one, reopening the dialog shows a stale red validation error, and closing via overlay keeps the half-typed email list.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:46 — (P2, conf 75) `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))` requires a user to be both admin AND owner, so team ADMINs (who see team bookings in the list and get the "Add guests" entry point at BookingListItem.tsx:194 with no permission gating) click it and always receive FORBIDDEN "you_do_not_have_permission" -- the UI entry point is shown to users who cannot use it.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/_router.tsx:79 — (P2, conf 50) The task asks for guest "management" but the change ships only an `addGuests` mutation: there is no remove-guest endpoint or UI, so a guest added by mistake (e.g. a typo'd address, which also got an AttendeeScheduledEmail invite) cannot be removed by the organizer, leaving the feature under-scoped against the stated intent.

packages/ui/index.tsx:153 — (P2, conf 50) `export { default as MultiEmail } from "./form/MultiEmailLazy";` adds a new public generic @calcom/ui form component (plus a Lazy wrapper) that has exactly one consumer (AddGuestsDialog) and re-implements the booking form-builder's existing "multiemail" field rendering (EmailField list + "add_another" + "Remove email" tooltip), creating a second divergent multi-email input in the design-system barrel beyond what the task needs.

packages/ui/form/MultiEmailLazy.tsx:3 — (P3, conf 50) The lazy wrapper's justification `/** These are like 40kb that not every user needs */` is copy-pasted from PhoneInputLazy, but MultiEmail only imports @calcom/ui primitives already in the bundle, so the `next/dynamic` indirection adds a loading flash in the dialog for no bundle saving and fails the deletion test (exporting ./form/MultiEmail directly behaves identically).

Additionally, `sendAddGuestsEmails` explicitly sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to any attendee whose email is in `newGuests` (i.e., newly added guests), which typically includes an iCal REQUEST invite. The finding’s UI-render condition for past bookings isn’t shown in this diff, but the backend behavior (no time check + sending scheduled invites) is directly verifiable here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts:5 — (P1, confidence 75) `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` has no `.max()` and the mutation has no rate limit, so any authorized caller can send one request with thousands of arbitrary addresses (and repeat it), making the platform send a "booking confirmed" email plus a CONFIRMED ICS invite to every address from the platform's sending domain under the organizer's display name, and also re-notifying every existing attendee and team member each time. This is an open spam relay.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `viewer.bookings.addGuests` mutation whose input schema is `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no size bound (`.max(...)`) (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts). The handler then (1) persists all provided emails via `attendees.createMany` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts) and (2) sends emails to organizer, team members, and *all* attendees via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (email-manager.ts). In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, every attendee triggers an outgoing email, and for emails in `newGuests` it sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` (i.e., a “scheduled/confirmed” style email with ICS) (packages/emails/email-manager.ts). With no request size cap shown in the diff, an authorized caller (organizer/team admin/owner/any attendee per handler permission checks) can submit a very large list and trigger large-volume outbound mail/ICS invites, repeating as desired. This is a security/spam-abuse risk directly enabled by the new endpoint; rate limiting is not visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:52 — (P1, confidence 75) `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` gives every attendee, including guests who were themselves added earlier, the same add-guest rights as the organizer, so one attendee can put arbitrary third parties on someone else's booking without the organizer's consent; those people then receive the meeting link, video password, location and the names/emails of all other attendees, and the organizer's calendar invite is changed. The emails go out under the organizer's name, and each added guest can add more guests, so access keeps widening.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, authorization explicitly allows any booking attendee: `const isAttendee = !!booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email);` and then permits the mutation when `isAttendee` is true (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw ...`). Since newly added guests are persisted as `booking.attendees` via `attendees.createMany`, any attendee whose email matches a logged-in user can call this endpoint to add more guests, which then triggers `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, widening access without organizer/admin restriction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:77 — (P2, confidence 100) `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` compares the raw guest string against a lowercased blacklist, so writing a blacklisted address with any uppercase letter (e.g. `Victim@Blocked.com`) gets past BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS, and the address is saved as an attendee and emailed.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is built as a lowercased list (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`), but the filter compares it against the raw `guest` string: `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. Since `includes` is case-sensitive and `guest` is not normalized (no `.toLowerCase()`), a blacklisted address entered with different casing can bypass the blacklist and be persisted/emailed, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:76 — (P3, confidence 75) the duplicate check `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive, so an existing attendee can be added again with different casing, creating a duplicate Attendee row and a second confirmation email and invite to the same inbox. Repeating this keeps sending mail to one victim.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the duplicate filtering uses a strict, case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and does not normalize either side (e.g., to lowercase). Since the input schema (`z.string().email()`) does not enforce lowercase, a user can submit `Test@Example.com` when `test@example.com` already exists and it will pass the filter, resulting in a duplicate attendee row via `attendees.createMany`. This can also trigger repeated calendar/email updates (the handler later calls `updateCalendarAttendees` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:168 — (P3, confidence 75) `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` passes the raw input list instead of `uniqueGuests`, so a caller who adds one new address plus existing attendees' emails makes `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` (email-manager.ts:541) send those existing attendees a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail "booking confirmed" message on every call. This lets a caller flood existing attendees with repeat confirmations.
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same underlying bug: sendAddGuestsEmails uses the full event attendees list to decide which email to send, but the membership test is against the raw input guests list (newGuests). This can misclassify existing attendees as “new” (or otherwise send the wrong template) and cause repeated AttendeeScheduledEmail/confirmation emails when existing addresses are included in the guests input.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:26 — (P2, confidence 50) the booking is loaded by id alone and its status and end time are never checked, so guests can be added to CANCELLED, REJECTED or past bookings, and the added addresses get a `status: "CONFIRMED"` invite and confirmation email for a meeting that is not happening. That gives abusers a way to send official-looking fake invites.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking is fetched with `prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })` and the handler proceeds to update attendees and send calendar/email updates without any check on booking state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) or timing (e.g., `endTime` in the past). The email templates used by `sendAddGuestsEmails` generate an ICS invite with `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`packages/emails/templates/*-add-guests-email.ts`) and `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called unconditionally, so the diff does support that guests could be added and receive official-looking confirmed invites even for bookings that arguably should no longer be modifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts:158 — (P2, confidence 50) `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })` use the caller's calendar credentials rather than the organizer's, so when an attendee or team admin calls this, `updateCalendarAttendees` sends the organizer's booking references through the caller's own calendar integrations. The organizer's real calendar event never gets the new guests, while the caller's integration is used to act on events it does not own.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, permissions allow non-organizers to call the mutation (`isAttendee` or `isTeamAdminOrOwner`). However, the calendar update is performed using the caller’s credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller). Then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` runs with that EventManager instance. From the diff alone, this means the organizer’s calendar integrations are not used for the update when the caller isn’t the organizer, which can result in the organizer’s actual calendar event not being updated (or an attempted update using an integration that doesn’t own the event).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts:25 — (P3, confidence 50) `replyTo` includes every attendee email, including addresses just injected by any attendee, so when the organizer or team members hit reply, their message goes to arbitrary third parties another attendee chose, leaking organizer correspondence.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`, the new organizer/team notification sets `replyTo: [this.calEvent.organizer.email, ...this.calEvent.attendees.map(({ email }) => email)]`, which includes *all* attendee emails. The diff also introduces `addGuestsHandler` where **any existing attendee** (`isAttendee`) is authorized to add guests, and the handler will `createMany` attendee records from the provided `guests` emails. That means an attendee can inject arbitrary third-party emails into `calEvent.attendees`, causing organizer/team “reply” actions to be addressed to those injected emails, leaking organizer correspondence to unintended recipients.
